question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>08</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> air is heated at constant volume through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The specific heat of air at constant volume is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>17</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kcal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>18</mn><mo> </mo><mi>joule</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cal</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The change in its internal energy is approximately.

solution.text:
The amount of work done for the given process should be zero, as the process is an isochoric process.

Thus, the change in internal energy will be equal to the heat exchanged in the process. Mathematically,

Q=∆U

Now,

∆U=ms∆T   ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

∆U=0.08×(170×4.18)×5 J≈ 284 J
